problem_summary.summary: Compact a non-decreasing integer array in place so each distinct value occurs once, preserving sorted order.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: sorted nums. Return the unique-prefix length k and place the distinct values in nums[0..k-1]; the suffix is ignored.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order

brute_force.explanation: Copy values into a temporary array only when they differ from the last copied value, then copy that prefix back into nums.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Sorted order places equal values together, so comparing with the last accepted value keeps exactly the first occurrence of each value.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) — each input value is checked once and the kept prefix is copied once.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary — the temporary array stores the distinct prefix.

optimized.explanation: Keep a write pointer at the next unique slot. Since nums is sorted, accept a read value only when it differs from the last written value.
optimized.correctness_idea: The write prefix contains one copy of every distinct value encountered in sorted order; a later duplicate cannot be needed again because equal values are contiguous.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary — compaction is performed in nums.

steps.action: Write 4 at index 2; write becomes 3 and is returned.

edge_cases.handling: The initial write length of 1 is returned.
Only the first value is kept.
Every value is already unique and the full length is returned.
